Looking at this, I need to compute the small/large ratio for each station (excluding station 30d where large=0 giving an undefined ratio), then find the median of these ratios.

**Ratios (small/large) by station, sorted:**
404.1, 522.1, 669.1, 709.8, 1273.5, 1460.6, 1640.1, 2520.0, 3692.1, 4140.9, **5133.2, 5340.4**, 8950.4, 9667.5, 11325.6, 17202.9, 18672.9, 18930.7, 27126.6, 40746.3, 96129.5, 629897.9

With 22 valid paired stations, the median is the average of the 11th and 12th values: (5133.2 + 5340.4) / 2 ≈ **5237**

The data come from the same stations/campaign in both PANGAEA datasets, so the size classes are directly paired and comparable, though the ratio spans several orders of magnitude (404 to ~630,000), reflecting the inherent right-skew of particle-size distributions.

answer.answer: Across 22 paired Weser stations (excluding one with zero large-particle counts), the small-particle (11-500 um) concentration exceeds the large-particle (500-5000 um) concentration by a median factor of about 5237.
